channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated reading: AI & geopolitics, chips, film & streaming, South African rugby

item.title: The monster Chris Hansen sees in Primetime, explained
item.description: Film analysis of the 'monster' motif in Primetime, the Chris Hansen / To Catch a Predator drama. Argues the creature reflects Hansen's own moral certainty and ratings desperation, and reads the film as a parallel to post-9/11 'with us or against us' thinking.

item.title: Designing Friction
item.description: A design manifesto arguing digital products should build in resistance, delay and discomfort as a counterweight to frictionless, algorithm-driven UX, in order to preserve human autonomy and deeper engagement.

item.title: How are countries evaluating AI models?
item.description: Brookings Institution analysis of how different governments approach testing and assessing AI models, and what the differing methods mean for international cooperation on AI governance.

item.title: Feeding the beast: Energy security as a precondition for the EU's AI power
item.description: Policy brief on how electricity access shapes the global AI race, covering Europe's energy costs, grid limits and import dependence, and how data centre siting might turn these constraints into a strength.

item.title: The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit
item.description: Survey of competing international AI governance efforts, including Chinese and US-led initiatives, UN processes and the EU AI Act, with recommendations for US policymakers ahead of bilateral talks.

item.title: TSMC, ASML eye 12-inch photomasks to unlock High-NA EUV's full-field potential
item.description: Report on TSMC and ASML exploring larger photomasks as a route to full-field High-NA EUV lithography for 2nm and angstrom-era nodes. The full text is paywalled.

item.title: Can a Radioactive Ore Break China's Grip on Rare Earths?
item.description: Looks at monazite as a possible source of rare earths outside China, weighing thorium waste handling, regulatory hurdles and the speculative dealmaking that has dogged the sector.

item.title: Why Everyone Is Talking About Hybrid Bonding, and Who Is in the Race
item.description: Explainer on hybrid bonding in advanced packaging, covering bonding methods, bottlenecks and the main suppliers as chip stacking and chiplets spread. Only part is free to read.

item.title: Bela Bajaria Was Fired Wednesday. Next Week Netflix Faces Wall Street
item.description: Reports on Netflix's content-chief change and roughly 1,000 job cuts, set against a weak stock year and expectations for the upcoming quarterly results. The article is partly paywalled.

item.title: Digger is Tom Cruise's worst box-office opening in 20 years, can lose $150 million
item.description: Breaks down the weak opening of Digger against its reported budget and marketing spend, and estimates how large the studio's eventual loss could be.

item.title: Disney Is Opening the Door to Netflix—and Changing the Streaming Playbook
item.description: Examines Disney's decision to license catalog titles to Netflix, tying it to falling linear TV revenue and debt, and compares the two companies' financials and valuations.

item.title: Bulls player ratings vs Stade Francais | 2026/27 Investec Champions Cup
item.description: Individual player ratings for the Bulls after their 56-20 Champions Cup opener at Loftus on 17 October.

item.title: Stormers thump Bristol despite first-half red card
item.description: Match report on the Stormers' 49-12 Champions Cup win over Bristol in Cape Town, achieved with a player sent off in the first half.

item.title: Springboks: Frans Malherbe issues 'hopeful' update after 19-month-long absence
item.description: Update on the Springbok prop's recovery, noting he has returned to non-contact team training with no decision yet on his future.

item.title: US-China race is on for the Gulf's AI future
item.description: An analysis of how Washington and Beijing compete to supply AI and digital infrastructure to Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and how Gulf states hedge between them. It considers the effect of the regional conflict on trust in US security guarantees.

item.title: Key watchdogs signal they will step up AI regulation
item.description: Looks at financial regulators and the UK moving toward closer oversight of AI models, set against a US administration with little appetite for tougher rules. Also touches on how China's approach to AI safety is characterised.

item.title: Why data centers are a top issue in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Commentary on why data center buildouts have become a campaign issue in both parties, tied to electricity prices, water use and wider affordability worries. Considers what the midterm results could mean for future AI infrastructure policy and investment.

item.title: What ASML Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
item.description: Summary of ASML's third-quarter results and outlook, covering EUV output plans, whether supply can keep up with AI-driven demand through 2028, and where High-NA adoption stands among its main customers.

item.title: Hot Chips 2026: Micron warns HBM wafer penalty is widening with every generation
item.description: Covers a Micron talk on how much more wafer area high-bandwidth memory consumes than standard DRAM and why that gap is growing. Connects it to memory pricing and supply tightness.

item.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
item.description: Weekly roundup spanning a packaging interposer deal between TSMC and GlobalFoundries, silicon carbide funding, nanoimprint and hyper-NA lithography developments, and industry sales and policy news.

item.title: How the Streamers Stack Up in Subscribers, Revenue and Profits
item.description: Side-by-side comparison of the major studios' streaming businesses using their latest quarterly figures for revenue, profit and subscribers. Also notes the status of the pending Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

item.title: Box Office Is Back. Now Comes the War Over Who Gets the Upside
item.description: Explains how talent profit participation, studio fees and streaming bonuses work as theatrical revenue recovers. Uses a low-budget hit as a case study in who gets paid when a film succeeds.

item.title: Netflix Is Out-Lobbying All of Hollywood
item.description: Data-driven look at 27 years of federal lobbying filings by the film industry, finding Netflix now outspends the MPA in Washington. Examines what each is lobbying for.

item.title: Stormers 49-12 Bristol Bears: Likely lads give Pat Lam's young side a lesson in finishing
item.description: Match report on the Stormers' bonus-point Champions Cup win over a young Bristol side in Cape Town, the most recent Stormers match. Notes Bristol's promise and their defensive lapses.

item.title: Lions' bravery in France speaks louder than Champions Cup defeat after Hyron Andrews' death
item.description: Opinion piece on the Lions' Champions Cup debut against La Rochelle, played after the death of lock Hyron Andrews, and the team's response on the day.

item.title: State of the URC: Wounded locals await Sharks, Lions
item.description: Early-season check on the four South African URC sides after round two, with the standings picture and a look ahead to the first local derbies.

item.title: AI Breakout Capacity: A Middle-Power Path Between Racing and Dependence
item.description: Carnegie paper on how countries without their own frontier AI labs, such as Germany, India and the UK, can hedge against losing access to American or Chinese models. It proposes keeping the legal authority and latent resources to mount a rapid catch-up push while staying aligned with a major supplier.

item.title: The Great Compute Reckoning: Record Chip Profits Collide with the Rising Cost of Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Commentary arguing that booming chipmaker earnings sit alongside growing strain in the credit and valuation side of the AI buildout. It frames chip supply, power, financing and geopolitics as increasingly linked.

item.title: Ten National AI Strategies Compared: Who Is Building, Who Is Stuck
item.description: Side-by-side look at the AI strategies of ten countries and regions, including Canada, the UK, the EU, Singapore, the UAE, Japan and South Korea. The common finding is that research foundations are in place but broad adoption across business and government lags.

item.title: Global 300mm Fab Equipment Spending to Reach $227 Billion in 2029 as Buildout Accelerates, SEMI Projects
item.description: Industry-group forecast of worldwide 300mm fab equipment spending, with a steep 2026 increase and continued double-digit growth through 2029. It also counts new fab construction starts by year, including several in the United States.

item.title: Japan to Inject Additional 400 Billion Yen Into Chipmaker Rapidus
item.description: Report on a fresh round of Japanese government equity for Rapidus, lifting total state backing. The money is meant to strengthen the balance sheet so the company can borrow heavily to scale 2nm production in Hokkaido.

item.title: Commentary: Samsung's US 2nm ramp faces no room for error
item.description: Commentary on whether Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab can reach volume 2nm production and narrow its gap with TSMC. It ties the outlook to anchor-customer timing, including Tesla and possible Broadcom orders. Partly paywalled.

item.title: It's True: Streamers Really Do Fire Executives Far Faster Than Studios
item.description: Data analysis of more than a thousand senior executive appointments at streaming services and legacy studios to compare how long leaders last. It uses Netflix's recent leadership exits as the jumping-off point.

item.title: The Skydance Film Enigma: How Do Paramount and Warner Bros. Coexist?
item.description: Analysis of how the combined Skydance-run company plans to operate two film studios and an unusually large release slate. It weighs the debt load and cost-cutting targets against sources' doubts that the output can be sustained.

item.title: Paramount Stock CRUSHED After Merger with Warner Discovery Closes
item.description: Critical newsletter take on the newly closed Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery combination, focusing on its debt, falling stock and bond prices and planned layoffs. It also questions whether the streaming strategy can be made profitable.

item.title: Bulls v Stade Francais: Five takeaways as 'hot' Springboks prospect's hat-trick and Rudolph 'magic' downs Parisians
item.description: Match analysis of the Bulls' Champions Cup opener at home to Stade Francais, picking out a young Springbok hopeful's three tries and the contribution of Jeandre Rudolph. Written as five key talking points from the win.

item.title: Butch: Smith is Lions' secret weapon
item.description: Former Springbok flyhalf Butch James discusses Lions captain Chris Smith's consistency and the team's forward development. He says the Lions must improve their away record, starting with upcoming URC trips to Scotland.

item.title: China considers export controls on AI, chips
item.description: Reports that Beijing is weighing limits on how far its AI models and chips can be sold or deployed abroad. Raises the question of whether such rules would be enforceable or merely a bargaining chip.

item.title: Trump Launches Super Intelligence Force + OpenAI Does More Math
item.description: Podcast episode from CSIS discussing the new US government AI initiative and recent OpenAI developments, from a policy angle.

item.title: The World Is Building Sovereign AI, It May Still Be Borrowing Control
item.description: Op-ed arguing that owning chips, cloud and models does not give a state real control over AI systems. Proposes practical safeguards such as mapped authority, fallback modes and workable provider switching.

item.title: AI Money Supercharges Semiconductor Research Labs
item.description: Looks at how chip and equipment makers are putting billions into private R&D on the back of AI demand, with Applied Materials' new California center as the example. Also covers how AI is used to speed up materials discovery and what it means for startups.

item.title: AI substrate bottleneck shifts from design to manufacturing
item.description: Industry report on advanced-package substrates, where the constraint on AI accelerators is moving from design work to actual production capacity.

item.title: Week 42, 2026
item.description: Weekly roundup spanning lithography and test equipment, record foundry results, silicon carbide supply deals and new packaging power-delivery approaches.

item.title: Netflix Revenue, Advertising Slowdown Rattles Wall Street as Growth Concerns Persist
item.description: Covers Netflix's third-quarter results: a profit beat on roughly $12.9B revenue, but a lowered ad-sales target and softer fourth-quarter growth outlook that pushed the shares down.

item.title: Hollywood's U.S. Production Share Plunges as Billions in Spending Move Abroad
item.description: Summarizes a union-backed EY study showing the share of studio scripted budgets spent on US shoots falling sharply for both film and TV since 1999. Frames the data in the debate over a federal production tax credit.

item.title: AMC Is Up 83% in 2026 and Cinemark Is Up 68%: Take Profits, or Hold On for the Ride?
item.description: Financial look at this year's rally in cinema-chain stocks versus the broader market. Weighs AMC's debt refinancing against its remaining leverage.

item.title: Emotional Lions come up short in Champions Cup as tributes paid to Andrews
item.description: Match report on the Lions' 31-14 loss at La Rochelle in their Champions Cup debut, played amid tributes to their late lock Hyron Andrews. La Rochelle led at the break and sealed a bonus point after half-time.

item.title: Stormers hand Bristol Bears a Champions Cup reality check
item.description: Match report on the Stormers' 49-12 Champions Cup opener against Bristol in Cape Town. They scored seven tries despite a red card and a sin-binning.

item.title: Rassie Erasmus Faces Injury Concerns as Key Springboks Stars Become Doubts for End of Year Tour
item.description: Rundown of injury doubts ahead of the Springboks' November tour, including Etzebeth, Kolbe and several long-term absentees, and what that means for selection.

item.title: China's outbound AI strategy starts with models and governance and ends with chips
item.description: Bruegel analysis of how China sequences its overseas AI push, leading with open-weight models and governance initiatives while its chips are not yet export-ready. It sets out what the authors think Europe should do in response.

item.title: Nvidia's China AI-chip share falls to 34% as Huawei reaches 28%
item.description: Reports IDC figures showing Nvidia's slice of China's AI data-center accelerator market shrinking while Huawei and other domestic vendors gain. Links the shift to US export restrictions and the growth of local chipmakers.

item.title: AI data centers are starved for power. Washington is scrambling to write new rules
item.description: Looks at how federal regulators, state agencies and utilities are struggling to set rules for connecting power-hungry AI data centers to the grid. Covers rising electricity bills, voter anger and likely legal fights over regulatory authority.

item.title: ASML Posts Record €11.7 Billion Q3 Sales as AI Demand Outruns Capacity
item.description: Summarises ASML's record third-quarter results and raised full-year outlook. Notes the company's warning that lithography supply for 2027 and 2028 may not meet customer demand.

item.title: ASML eyes hybrid bonding, report finds, as Chinese firms adopt chip packaging technique
item.description: Covers a SemiAnalysis report on ASML's patent filings and development work on hybrid bonding tools, a move from lithography into back-end packaging. Also notes growing adoption of the technique among Chinese chip companies.

item.title: Chinese startup presents 15-watt EUV source prototype
item.description: Describes a Tsinghua-linked startup's prototype EUV light source and its claimed output. Explains why the figures are hard to compare with ASML's sources and why the device looks suited to research rather than production.

item.title: The Problem With Hollywood's Plan to Make Netflix Share the Wealth
item.description: Examines a new Hollywood lobbying push for Congress to require big streamers to spend a share of original-content budgets on independent producers, modeled on old fin-syn rules. Considers the legal and regulatory hurdles. Partly paywalled.

item.title: DC's 'Clayface' Cost $30 Million. Is This How to Fix Superhero Hell?
item.description: Looks at DC's bet on a low-budget, R-rated Batman-villain film as a way to keep using comic-book IP without large downside risk. Questions whether a lesser-known character can succeed. Partly paywalled.

item.title: State of the URC: Bulls, Stormers flex muscles
item.description: Roundup of the latest United Rugby Championship round for the South African sides, including the Bulls and Stormers wins and how returning Springboks lifted them. Covers where they now sit on the log.

item.title: Can the UK drive middle power coordination on AI?
item.description: A Chatham House fellow argues the UK should help middle powers coordinate on frontier AI rather than lean on Washington, pointing to a multi-country statement on frontier controls and its 2027 G20 presidency. The piece also weighs how US and Chinese pressure could complicate such efforts.

item.title: America's Preemption Gamble
item.description: Contrasts a June 2026 House discussion draft that would pair federal safety duties for large AI developers with a pause on state rules against the EU's enforcement of its AI Act. The author argues federal standards should be a floor states can exceed, not a ceiling.

item.title: The Silicon Fault Line: How Chips, Power and the Law Are Redrawing the Map of Global Power
item.description: Argues that rivalry over chips and AI compute now spans knowledge, manufacturing, enforcement, demand and energy, not just export controls. It draws on recent moves in China, Taiwan, Europe and the UK data-centre power debate.

item.title: Infineon and Wolfspeed sign new multi-year 200mm silicon carbide wafer supply deal
item.description: Reports that Infineon's silicon carbide substrate supply from Wolfspeed moves from 150mm to 200mm wafers under a new multi-year agreement. It ties the shift to demand from AI data centers, EVs, solar inverters and industrial drives.

item.title: Intel installs production tools at Fab 62 in Arizona, provides updates on Ohio chip fab
item.description: Covers Intel starting equipment installation at its Arizona Fab 62, a late-2028 operational target, and construction progress at its Ohio site. It also notes the company's statements on High-NA EUV use in volume production.

item.title: Chip Industry Week In Review (Oct. 16)
item.description: Weekly roundup spanning new fabs, packaging and test partnerships, China memory and EUV-source developments, TSMC and ASML results, and policy and supply-chain items.

item.title: A Private Equity Reckoning After Hello Sunshine's Fall — and Who Wins
item.description: Examines the sale of Hello Sunshine back to its founder at a small fraction of its 2021 private-equity valuation. It asks what the markdown means for other star-led production companies and where investor capital goes next.

item.title: Fall box office slows with two flops: 'Digger' and 'The Social Reckoning'
item.description: Looks at a weak fall weekend, including a steep second-weekend drop and large projected losses for a big-budget Tom Cruise film. It contrasts a soft sequel opening with a modestly budgeted horror title that led the chart.

item.title: Bester snatches dramatic Sharks win
item.description: Match report on the Sharks' 40-33 Challenge Cup win at Lyon, decided by a try after the final hooter following a late Lyon equaliser.

item.title: Sharks ride Lyon momentum into tough Cardiff test
item.description: Previews the Sharks' URC trip to Cardiff after the Lyon win, looking at the set-piece matchup and the expected kicking-heavy, difficult-conditions contest.

item.title: SA's URC teams face northern examination as club season ramps up
item.description: Surveys how South Africa's four URC sides stand early in 2026/27, with all in the top half, and the demanding away fixtures awaiting the Sharks and Lions.

item.title: SemiAnalysis Pegs China Datacenter Capacity at 24GW, US at 56GW
item.description: Summarises SemiAnalysis's new model of China's data-centre buildout, comparing delivered capacity with the US and noting that chip supply rather than power is the binding limit. Also covers the tenants renting that capacity and the capex of China's biggest tech firms.

item.title: Competing AI strategies for the US and China
item.description: Congressional testimony comparing how Washington and Beijing are pursuing AI, with China taking a full-stack, application-focused approach. It weighs what export controls have and haven't achieved and what the US should prioritise at home.

item.title: How can Europe address its pressing artificial-intelligence compute infrastructure shortfall?
item.description: A policy brief sizing the EU's share of global AI compute against the US and China, and arguing that permitting speed and grid access matter more than money. It critiques sovereignty rules and subsidy design and proposes alternatives.

item.title: Why TSMC is Turning to GlobalFoundries for CoWoS Interposers
item.description: Explains why TSMC is outsourcing part of its advanced-packaging interposer supply to a mature-node foundry. Covers the timing, the qualification and yield caveats, and why it is a medium-term capacity fix.

item.title: Japan's $15 billion Rapidus chip bet hinges on winning customers
item.description: Looks at Japan's state-backed 2-nanometre foundry effort and its push to line up design partners before production starts. Analysts quoted question whether real customer demand and stable yields will follow.

item.title: SEMI Forecasts 11.8% Growth in Silicon Wafer Shipments in 2026, With Record Highs Expected through 2029
item.description: Industry-group forecast for silicon wafer volumes through 2029, with AI-driven demand for epitaxial and memory wafers as the main driver. Gives the yearly shipment outlook and what the figures include.

item.title: Why Nielsen Keeps Publishing 'The Gouge'
item.description: Commentary on Nielsen's monthly Gauge and doubts about its streaming-versus-linear comparisons. Considers how the reports affected ad negotiations and why a recalibration was delayed.

item.title: When to Stream's Weekly Tracking Report - 10/16/26
item.description: A weekly tracker of upcoming digital and PVOD dates for studio films, useful for comparing how long each studio waits after theatrical release. Notes which titles moved sooner after weak box office.

item.title: Sharks player ratings: Springboks-in-waiting wreak havoc as teenager and bullish forward shine in victory over Cardiff
item.description: Player-by-player ratings for the Sharks' URC win at Cardiff on 23 October, the most recent South African match. Highlights the standout performers in the 36-21 result.

item.title: How Boks' next generation shapes up leading to 2027 World Cup
item.description: Opinion piece on how Rassie Erasmus is building Springbok depth gradually rather than replacing veterans wholesale. Reviews recent debutants and who looks set to form the next core group.

item.title: I Listened to Over 7 Hours of Peter Thiel's Leaked Antichrist Lectures. They're Surprisingly Libertarian.
item.description: A close read of Peter Thiel's lecture series on the Antichrist, focused on how his warnings about world government and technology regulation fit or clash with libertarian thinking. Includes his views on empire, financial surveillance and individual choice.

item.title: Trump 2.0 Runs on Tech Accelerationism
item.description: Essay tracing how accelerationist ideas moved from fringe circles into Silicon Valley and the second Trump administration. Argues AI deployment in government concentrates power and weakens democratic accountability.

item.title: Religion: Thiel's 'Antichrist' obsession
item.description: Roundup of critical reactions to Thiel's Antichrist lectures, from historians and clergy to commentators on his own influence. Useful as a quick map of the main objections to his framing of AI and regulation.

item.title: America's AI Action Plan After One Year: What the Administration Has Done, and What Comes Next
item.description: An audit of how far the US AI Action Plan's many recommendations have progressed a year on. Finds most show partial movement, largely through guidance and announcements, with built infrastructure and procurement results still pending.

item.title: The national security implications of building frontier AI data centers overseas
item.description: A scoping paper arguing that where advanced AI infrastructure is hosted is now a security question as well as a commercial one. It sketches risks such as sabotage, foreign legal access and host-country leverage, and previews a research series on which workloads belong where.

item.title: How a surge in defence and dual-use technology investment could reconfigure the global AI race
item.description: A research paper on four trends, including military AI funding, tighter tech-government ties and sovereign AI efforts, that could fragment a field now led by the US and China. Also weighs valuation-bubble risks and offers recommendations for private-sector actors.

item.title: [News] Musk Targets Terafab Chip Volume Production in 3Q28, First SRAM Test Chip by Mid-2027
item.description: Covers the timeline for Musk's Terafab venture, with a test chip planned in Austin before volume output. Highlights equipment supply from ASML and US toolmakers and the unresolved roles of TSMC and Intel as the main hurdles.

item.title: Foundries And OSATs Increasingly Overlap
item.description: Explains how limited foundry capacity is pushing advanced back-end work such as 2.5D and panel-level assembly toward outsourced assembly and test providers. Describes the resulting blurring of the line between the two business models.

item.title: Japan Offers GlobalFoundries $21B for U.S. Fab Expansion
item.description: Looks at a Japanese financing pledge for two new fabs at GlobalFoundries' New York site and the claimed boost to US capacity. Notes analyst concerns about the company's growing reliance on government backing.

item.title: Wall Street Bets on Box Office Resurgence
item.description: Looks at how a strong 2026 box office and a rally in exhibitor stocks are shaping analyst forecasts for 2027 and 2028. Compares more bullish and more cautious views on how much upside remains.

item.title: Netflix's Peter Rice Risk: Studio Insider, But Streaming Outsider
item.description: Assesses Netflix's choice of a veteran broadcast and studio executive to run global content, using views from former colleagues and rivals. Weighs his talent relationships against limited experience with data-driven streaming as the service faces share and cost pressures.

item.title: Netflix Explains How It Will Fix Its Growth Problem. Wall Street Isn't Convinced
item.description: Analysis of Netflix's slowest revenue growth in years and the levers management says it will pull, including licensing, add-ons and advertising. Explains why investors and analysts remain skeptical.

item.title: Bulls player ratings: Springboks star puts pressure on Rassie Erasmus while Marcell Coetzee 'punishes' Ulster
item.description: Individual ratings for the Bulls after their 34-26 URC win over Ulster at Loftus Versfeld, the most recent match played. Picks out standout Springbok-level performances relevant to national selection.

item.title: Sharks trounce Cardiff, but suffer Giant loss
item.description: Match report on the Sharks' six-try, bonus-point URC win away to Cardiff. Also covers captain Andre Esterhuizen's early injury and what it could mean for the Springboks' end-of-year matches.

item.title: Sharks bring back 3 Springboks for URC mission against 'quality team'
item.description: Team news ahead of the Sharks' trip to Cardiff, with three Springboks recalled and Esterhuizen back as captain. Includes the coaching staff's view of the opposition.

item.title: US Tech Searches for Rules on AI: China Already Has Them
item.description: A UCL academic traces the stages of China's AI regulation up to its latest safety governance framework. She weighs what that means for the US market-led approach.

item.title: Tokenpolitik: How the United States Can Compete with China to Build the Global AI Stack
item.description: CSIS commentary framing US-China AI competition as a contest over infrastructure exports. It proposes a coordinated government strategy for financing and partnering on datacenters and power abroad.

item.title: A summer of AI summits reveals a widening US-China divide
item.description: Briefing guide surveying the international AI governance meetings of summer 2026 and the competing US and Chinese initiatives. It closes with discussion questions on where the divide could deepen.

item.title: Intel CTO: EUV Tool Shortage Caps AI Chip Supply Growth at Roughly Double
item.description: Reports an Intel executive's argument that limited EUV lithography tool output constrains how fast advanced chip supply can grow. It covers ASML delivery pace, lead times and other bottlenecks.

item.title: Lam Research Sinks 9% as Supply Constraints Cap Outlook; Applied Materials Drops 6%, ASML Holding Falls 4%
item.description: Covers Lam Research's record quarter, its cautious guidance tied to supply constraints, and the sell-off across equipment makers. Includes the company's early view of 2027 fab equipment spending and China exposure.

item.title: How and When the Memory Chip Shortage Will End
item.description: Explains why AI demand for high-bandwidth memory has tightened DRAM supply and how new fabs and packaging advances might ease it. Discusses timelines and the risk of a later bust.

item.title: Netflix and Disney Are Scrambling to Survive
item.description: Argues that Netflix and Disney are restructuring as Paramount closes its Warner Bros. Discovery deal. Covers layoffs, a licensing partnership and the political backdrop.

item.title: Stormers player ratings: Springboks rookie leads from the front in crazy triumph against the Scarlets
item.description: Player-by-player ratings for the Stormers after their high-scoring URC win over the Scarlets on 24 October.

item.title: It's official: Kwagga's a Bull
item.description: Reports the Bulls signing Springbok loose forward Kwagga Smith from Japan on a three-year deal. Covers his injury timeline and the coach's comments.

item.title: The Gulf has billions to spend on AI. It still needs Nvidia
item.description: Looks at Saudi Arabia and the UAE trying to diversify AI chip purchases beyond one supplier. Explains how weaker alternatives, US export rules, shared supply bottlenecks and software lock-in keep them reliant on Nvidia.

item.title: EU AI Act's High-Risk Deadline: Deferred, Not Cancelled
item.description: A research note on the Digital Omnibus regulation that pushed back compliance dates for high-risk AI systems into 2027 and 2028. It sets out which obligations, such as general-purpose model rules and prohibited practices, stay on their original timelines.

item.title: Will China Crack Down on Open-Weight Models?
item.description: An analysis of Beijing's tension between promoting open-weight AI and tightening security control. Considers why restrictions haven't come yet and which kinds of incidents could change that.

item.title: Large-Format Masks Move From Aspiration To Industry Roadmap
item.description: Reports on an industry survey and panel about moving to larger photomasks for High-NA EUV lithography. Discusses the 2031 pilot-line goal and the single-source suppliers and process hurdles that must line up first.

item.title: [News] After TSMC's 3Q26 Earnings: Key Brokerage Takeaways as 2028 Capex Forecasts Reach US$105B
item.description: Summarizes how foreign brokerages read TSMC's latest quarter, including raised growth outlooks and higher capital-spending estimates for 2027-2028. Notes margin pressure from the 2nm ramp as the main concern.

item.title: Hanmi Semiconductor Cements TC Bonder Leadership at SEMICON West as HBM4 Orders Surge
item.description: Profiles Hanmi's thermal compression bonding tools for high-bandwidth memory stacking, shown at SEMICON West. Covers its market position, a large SK hynix order and its expansion plans.

item.title: What to know about the landmark Warner Bros. Discovery sale
item.description: A timeline of Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, from the competing Netflix bid through regulatory approval, state litigation and closing. Highlights the combined company's debt load and expected cost cuts.

item.title: Paramount Shows Streaming Progress as it Tiptoes Around Warner Bros. Merger Lawsuit
item.description: Reviews Paramount's second-quarter results, with streaming profit rising on Paramount+ growth. Also covers executives' confidence in the Warner Bros. Discovery deal despite a legal challenge and a trial set for 2027.

item.title: Box Office Is Bad. Streaming Films Are So-So. I Have a Win-Win Solution
item.description: A data-driven argument from Entertainment Strategy Guy that big straight-to-streaming films left substantial box office money on the table. Weighs theatrical versus streaming outcomes for studios and talent.

item.title: Bulls make heavy weather of Ulster win
item.description: Match report on the Bulls' URC home win over Ulster at Loftus Versfeld. Describes the early lead, Ulster's second-half fightback and the late kick that settled it.

item.title: Everitt's Edinburgh stay top as Lions crumble in Scotland
item.description: Match report on the Lions' round-four URC defeat at Edinburgh. Covers the close first half and the home side's second-half try surge that kept them unbeaten.

item.title: SA Rugby's R2bn commercial rise after record sponsorship revenues
item.description: Looks at SA Rugby's sponsorship revenue overtaking broadcast income for the first time. Explains the bundled commercial model and key partners such as Airlink and Pick n Pay.

item.title: The $10 trillion question: Financing the AI buildout
item.description: Podcast episode discussing a Brookings paper that projects roughly $10 trillion of US AI data-center, power and chip spending through 2032. Looks at how joint ventures, leases and private credit finance it and why disclosure matters.

item.title: Speed Isn't Working as an AI Strategy. The U.S. Has a Better Option.
item.description: Argues that a speed-first US AI strategy is getting harder to sustain as risks mount. Proposes building national strength through institutions and societal resilience instead.

item.title: AI is sprinting past human control. Can testing and evaluation catch up?
item.description: Examines weaknesses in how frontier AI models are tested, from contaminated benchmarks to models that game evaluations. Makes the case for a national assurance system and international cooperation.

item.title: Glass substrate roadmaps examined: Absolics in final qualification and a first product that keeps slipping
item.description: Reviews where glass-core packaging substrates stand across Absolics, Samsung, TSMC, Intel and others. Notes repeated schedule slips and the milestones to watch.

item.title: How 'You Can See Everything' Shattered Box Office Records
item.description: Explains how A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary posted one of the biggest documentary openings in years. Credits a secretive marketing campaign, its star's online following and strong audience scores.

item.title: "Digger" To Lose Warner's $150 Million?
item.description: Summarises projections that Warner Bros.' Tom Cruise film could be 2026's biggest box-office loss. Covers the weak projected opening and the estimated deficit.

item.title: Crocked Boks a blessing in disguise
item.description: Column arguing that injuries to senior Springboks give the coach a chance to test new combinations and younger players. Names several emerging talents who deserve a look.

item.title: URC roundup: Three out of four for SA teams as they count the injury cost
item.description: Round-up of the South African sides' URC weekend, with three wins and a heavy Lions defeat in Edinburgh. Also tallies the injuries picked up by several squads.

item.title: Analysis: China's new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels
item.description: Explains a draft Chinese rule set that would restrict transfers of core AI technology while leaving access to Chinese models through websites and cloud services, with public comment open into November.

item.title: Intel Advances Arizona and Ohio Fabs and Confirms High-NA EUV in Production
item.description: Covers tool installation at Intel's Arizona Fab 62, construction progress in Ohio, and the company's statement that High-NA EUV is now part of its volume manufacturing plans.

item.title: Biggest Streaming Movies Q3 Shock: Peacock Tops
item.description: Newsletter item on Nielsen's Q3 streaming-movie rankings, comparing first-weeks viewing of theatrical titles across Peacock, Disney+, Netflix and Prime Video, plus other industry business notes.

item.title: Rassie injects talented youth into Springbok squad for Nations Championship finale
item.description: Looks at the 37-man Springbok squad for the November Nations Championship matches, its uncapped additions and the injury absences behind the selections.

item.title: Sovereignty by the Megawatt: The New Geopolitics of Supercomputing - Part IV
item.description: Surveys October supercomputing announcements across Germany, the US, India, France and Sweden and argues compute is spreading across jurisdictions while accelerator supply stays concentrated. Also raises energy-grid, post-quantum security and access-allocation concerns.

item.title: 26 State AGs Urge Congress to Regulate Frontier AI and Preserve State Authority
item.description: A law-firm blog explains a bipartisan letter from 26 state attorneys general seeking federal frontier-AI rules without preempting state enforcement. It lays out the six elements the coalition wants in any national framework.

item.title: ASML says 2027 and 2028 supply will fall short of demand as Q3 sales hit a record
item.description: Summarizes ASML's record third quarter, its fourth-quarter and full-year guidance, and its warning that planned 2027-28 lithography capacity will not cover customer demand. Notes the services business lifting margins.

item.title: From Wafers to Panels: Overcoming Lithography Challenges in Advanced Packaging
item.description: Equipment engineers explain why packaging lithography prioritizes overlay accuracy, throughput and thermal stability over feature shrink as substrates move from wafers to large panels. Describes stage design approaches to limit drift.

item.title: From Process Learning To Production Control: Trends In Advanced Packaging And Implications To Characterization And Test
item.description: A vendor presentation on how 2.5D, CoWoS, hybrid bonding and 3D stacking create yield and defect issues unlike front-end logic. Outlines an analytics and metrology approach to ramping packaging processes.

item.title: 2026 Box Office Could Top $28 Billion By End Of Year
item.description: Tallies year-to-date domestic and worldwide grosses against post-Covid records and pre-pandemic benchmarks, then projects year-end totals. Considers why even a record year trails the 2010s.

item.title: Stormers outlast Scarlets 52-40 in wild Cape Town clash
item.description: Match report on a 14-try URC game in Cape Town in which the Stormers built a big first-half lead, were pegged back level, and won through late tries.

item.title: OPINION: Kwagga's return highlights SA's bloated loosie state
item.description: A column on Kwagga Smith's move to the Bulls and what the depth of loose forwards at South African URC sides means for players seeking game time.

item.title: Samsung to Use TSMC for Base Die in Nvidia's Custom HBM
item.description: Reports that Nvidia is asking memory makers to standardize on a common base-die process and core DRAM node for its custom high-bandwidth memory. Covers what that means for Samsung's foundry unit and its dependence on TSMC capacity.

item.title: State of the URC: Sharks bite, Lions bruised
item.description: Round-four review of the South African sides in the United Rugby Championship, with the Bulls, Stormers and Sharks collecting bonus-point wins while the Lions slipped. Includes the standings picture and a look ahead to round five.
